<!-- Source: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (2009), section 2.4, eq. 2.9, p. 18,
     and p. 19 for the median remark.
     The name "risk" is standard terminology and is not used on those pages. -->

:::{#def-risk}
#### Risk (expected loss)

For a random variable $Y$
and a prediction $\hat{y}$
(a constant, or a function $f(X)$ of a random input $X$),
the **risk** is the expectation of the loss:

$$R \eqdef \E{L(Y, \hat{y})}$$

For squared error loss and a prediction $f(X)$,
the risk is called the **expected prediction error**:

$$\operatorname{EPE}(f) \eqdef \E{\sqf{Y - f(X)}}$$

:::

::: notes

In @exr-loss (parts 2 and 3),
the expected squared error loss is $5$ for the prediction $c = 1$,
and $4$ for the prediction $c = 2$.

Replacing squared error loss by absolute error loss
changes the best prediction from the conditional mean to the conditional median.
This statement is from @hastie2009elements [p. 19],
without proof here.

:::
